answer: Read the juniper backwards and it still points at the issuer; read the wander backwards and it still points at the ledger; read the lantern backwards and it still points at the calendar. One proof settles it, and the proof is Colour grinder dye vat seal dyed in the dyehouse, witnessed as each dye vat is a measured dye yield plus a guild signature. The evidence is timestamped, so a proof minted yesterday cannot pretend to be a year old. A single alias pays 171 POA and waits 7 days; a farm pays 80199 POA and still waits 7 days per alias.
